name: Dysarthria–clumsy hand syndrome
presentation: Speech becomes slurred and the patient complains that one hand has become clumsy: writing deteriorates and fine tasks are fumbled, although strength is nearly normal. Examination shows facial weakness of the lower face, tongue deviation, mild hand weakness with hyperreflexia and clumsiness, and sometimes an extensor plantar. Sensation is intact.

deficits.sign: Dysarthria with lower facial weakness and tongue deviation
Clumsiness and mild weakness of the hand with hyperreflexia
Impaired fine finger movements and dysmetria

reasoning: This is a small-vessel infarct in the paramedian basis pontis or the genu of the internal capsule, where the corticobulbar fibers to the facial and hypoglossal nuclei run beside the corticospinal fibers for the hand. The corticobulbar fibers cross at the level of the nuclei in the pons and medulla, and the corticospinal fibers cross in the pyramidal decussation, so both the facial weakness and the hand signs are contralateral to the lesion. Involvement of the corticopontocerebellar pathway, which crosses twice like all cerebellar loops, adds the clumsiness on the same side as the weakness. The lesion is too small to reach the sensory pathways in the pontine tegmentum or the posterior capsule, and the cortex is intact, so there is no sensory loss, aphasia or field defect. It is really a fragment of the pure motor syndrome in which the face and hand fibers, which lie most anteriorly in the capsule and most medially in the crus and pons, are picked out by an even smaller infarct.

imagingFindings.finding: Small (under 15 mm) focus of restricted diffusion in the paramedian basis pontis or genu of the internal capsule; CT is often normal in the first day.
Small CSF-intensity cavity with a FLAIR-bright rim, often multiple, with diffuse white matter hyperintensity of small vessel disease.

commonCauses: Hypertensive lipohyalinosis of a single perforating artery

mimics.name: Cortical branch infarct
mimics.howToDistinguish: Cortical signs (aphasia, neglect, field loss, gaze deviation) exclude a lacune

management: Antiplatelet therapy, statin and blood pressure control
Thrombolysis when presenting within the window and disabling
Early mobilization; prognosis for recovery is good
